From 98ef2046f28b642ad35935972a173194ea58a21d Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Denis Efremov <efremov@linux.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jul 2019 20:54:56 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] mm: remove the exporting of totalram_pages

Previously totalram_pages was the global variable.  Currently,
totalram_pages is the static inline function from the include/linux/mm.h
However, the function is also marked as EXPORT_SYMBOL, which is at best an
odd combination.  Because there is no point for the static inline function
from a public header to be exported, this commit removes the
EXPORT_SYMBOL() marking.  It will be still possible to use the function in
modules because all the symbols it depends on are exported.

Link: http://lkml.kernel.org/r/20190710141031.15642-1-efremov@linux.com
Fixes: ca79b0c211af6 ("mm: convert totalram_pages and totalhigh_pages variables to atomic")
Signed-off-by: Denis Efremov <efremov@linux.com>
Acked-by: Michal Hocko <mhocko@suse.com>
Cc: Vlastimil Babka <vbabka@suse.cz>
Cc: Oscar Salvador <osalvador@suse.de>
Cc: Pavel Tatashin <pavel.tatashin@microsoft.com>
Cc: Mel Gorman <mgorman@techsingularity.net>
Cc: Mike Rapoport <rppt@linux.ibm.com>
Cc: Alexander Duyck <alexander.h.duyck@linux.intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>

diff --git a/mm/page_alloc.c b/mm/page_alloc.c
index 8e3bc949ebcc..060303496094 100644
--- a/mm/page_alloc.c
+++ b/mm/page_alloc.c
@@ -224,8 +224,6 @@ int sysctl_lowmem_reserve_ratio[MAX_NR_ZONES] = {
 	[ZONE_MOVABLE] = 0,
 };
 
-EXPORT_SYMBOL(totalram_pages);
-
 static char * const zone_names[MAX_NR_ZONES] = {
 #ifdef CONFIG_ZONE_DMA
 	 "DMA",
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `mm/page_alloc.c`**
   - The line `EXPORT_SYMBOL(totalram_pages);` has been removed. This change indicates that the `totalram_pages` function, which is now a static inline function, will no longer be exported for use in loadable kernel modules.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `mm/page_alloc.c` is a direct response to the change in the status of `totalram_pages` from a global variable to a static inline function. By removing the `EXPORT_SYMBOL` marking, the patch clarifies that it is unnecessary to export a static inline function from a public header, as it can still be utilized in modules through other exported symbols it depends on. This aligns with the goal of maintaining clean and efficient code by avoiding the export of symbols that do not need to be publicly accessible.

However, the function is also marked as EXPORT_SYMBOL, which is at best an
odd combination.  Because there is no point for the static inline function
from a public header to be exported, this commit removes the
EXPORT_SYMBOL() marking.  It will be still possible to use the function in
modules because all the symbols it depends on are exported.

Link: http://lkml.kernel.org/r/20190710141031.15642-1-efremov@linux.com
Fixes: ca79b0c211af6 ("mm: convert totalram_pages and totalhigh_pages variables to atomic")
Signed-off-by: Denis Efremov <efremov@linux.com>

Cc: Mel Gorman <mgorman@techsingularity.net>
Cc: Mike Rapoport <rppt@linux.ibm.com>
Cc: Alexander Duyck <alexander.h.duyck@linux.intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>

Here is the root cause:
The root cause of the bug was the unnecessary export of the `totalram_pages` function, which was defined as a static inline function. Exporting a static inline function is considered an odd combination because it is not intended for public use, leading to potential confusion and misuse in kernel modules. This could result in improper dependencies and linkage issues, as the function should not be accessible outside its intended scope.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
static inline unsigned long totalram_pages(void) { ... }
EXPORT_SYMBOL(totalram_pages);
```
Reason:
The `totalram_pages` function is defined as a static inline function, which means it is intended for use only within the compilation unit it is defined in. However, marking it with `EXPORT_SYMBOL` allows it to be accessed from outside this scope, leading to potential misuse and confusion in kernel modules, as it creates improper dependencies.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
-EXPORT_SYMBOL(totalram_pages);
```
Reason:
Removing the `EXPORT_SYMBOL(totalram_pages);` statement prevents the `totalram_pages` function from being accessible outside its intended scope, aligning its usage with its definition as a static inline function. This eliminates the potential for confusion and misuse in kernel modules, ensuring that the function is only used where it is defined.
